name: Prince Edward Island
summary: A gold lion on red in the upper part, above a large oak tree and three oak saplings on a green island, with a border of alternating red and white rectangles on three sides.
origin: The arms were granted in 1905. The flag, a banner of the arms with an added border, was adopted on 24 March 1964, the centenary of the Charlottetown Conference that led to Confederation.

symbols.name: Lion
symbols.description: A gold lion passant guardant on red.
symbols.meaning: England, and Prince Edward, Duke of Kent, after whom the island is named.

symbols.name: Oak and three saplings
symbols.description: A large oak and three small oaks on an island.
symbols.meaning: The large oak is England; the saplings are the island's three counties, sheltering under it. The motto is 'Parva sub ingenti' (The small under the protection of the great).

facts: The 1864 Charlottetown Conference was the first step to Canadian Confederation.
Its border of alternating colours is unusual among Canadian flags.
clues: A gold lion above a large oak and three saplings, with a red and white border.
Its three saplings are three counties.
Adopted for the centenary of a conference that led to a country's founding.
